title: Transition metals
group: CHEM-ATOM / CHEM-PER — Atoms & the Periodic Table
examples: What makes transition metals different from other metals?
Can you give an example of a transition metal used as a catalyst?
Why are transition metals often coloured?

explain.say: Transition metals are a group of elements found in the middle of the periodic table. They show many different chemical properties.
Another key property is that they are usually good conductors of electricity. They also tend to form positive ions easily.

items: Are usually solid at room temperature

explain.say: These metals are often used as catalysts because they speed up chemical reactions without being used up themselves. Platinum is a common example.
Transition metals often form ions that have distinct colours. This is because the electrons in the d-orbitals absorb specific wavelengths of light.
In everyday life, transition metals are used in batteries because they conduct electricity very well. Copper wiring in your house is a common example.
A common mistake is thinking all metals are good electrical conductors. However, some non-metal elements are also conductors in certain states.

faq.q: What is the difference between a catalyst and a reactant?
faq.a: A catalyst speeds up a reaction without being chemically changed itself. Reactants are the substances that start the chemical change.
asks: Does a catalyst get used up?
What is the role of a catalyst in a reaction?

faq.q: Why are transition metal ions often coloured?
faq.a: The colour comes from electrons in the d-orbitals absorbing specific amounts of visible light. The colour we see is the light that is not absorbed.
asks: Where does the colour in metal ions come from?
What causes the visible colour of transition metal salts?

faq.q: Are all transition metals good electrical conductors?
faq.a: Most transition metals are excellent conductors of electricity. However, some non-metal allotropes can also conduct electricity.
asks: Is conductivity a property of all transition metals?

faq.q: Can transition metals form compounds with different colours?
faq.a: Yes, they can. The colour of the compound often depends on the oxidation state or the ligands attached to the metal ion.
asks: Does the colour change if the metal ion changes state?
What affects the colour of a transition metal compound?

faq.q: What is the general property of malleability for these metals?
faq.a: Malleability means the metal can be hammered into thin sheets without breaking. This is a common physical property.
asks: Can these metals be beaten into sheets?
What does it mean for a metal to be malleable?

facts: Transition metals are generally good conductors of electricity.
They often act as catalysts in industrial chemical processes.
The colour of transition metal ions is due to d-orbital electron transitions.
Properties include being malleable and ductile.

quiz.say: Which property is most commonly used to describe the ability of copper to carry electrical current?
quiz.why: Copper is a classic example of a transition metal known for its excellent electrical conductivity.

wrong.0: Most transition metals are solids, making this property incorrect for the group as a whole.
wrong.1: Transition metals are generally excellent conductors of heat, not poor conductors.
wrong.3: While some are reactive, conductivity is a more defining and measurable property for common uses.

quiz.say: If an ion has a distinct blue colour, which property are you likely observing?
quiz.why: The colour in transition metal ions comes specifically from the arrangement and behaviour of electrons in the d-orbitals.

wrong.0: While oxidation state matters, the specific electronic structure of the d-orbitals is the direct cause of the colour.
wrong.1: Although the solvent affects the colour, the intrinsic property comes from the metal ion itself.
wrong.2: Temperature can affect colour, but the fundamental reason for the colour is electronic structure.

quiz.say: Which substance is best suited for speeding up a reaction without being consumed?
quiz.why: Catalysts, often transition metals, lower the activation energy of a reaction, speeding it up without being used up.

wrong.0: Strong acids can sometimes act as catalysts, but transition metals are the specific focus here.
wrong.1: Reactants are what are consumed in the reaction, not what speeds it up.
wrong.2: Heat energy increases rate, but a catalyst changes the path, not just the energy input.
